title: About to put the following autonomous strategy in play with $15,000. Looking for feedback on my prompt and any experienced opinions about how the intention of my strategy might clash with reality (like stop losses getting triggered so often that I blow up the account instead of preserving capital.)
author: Independent_One_5568
selftext:
Act as an automated options trading agent. Monitor a targeted watchlist consisting strictly of the following tickers: AMZN, GOOG, META, MSFT, TSLA, NVDA, TSM, SPCX, and AAPL. We will be opening call options every trading day, unless we have a previously purchased option that has not yet been closed. In this case, the goal will be to close the previously purchased contract.

The agent must operate under a strict single-asset daily concentration limit: Once the agent selects a single underlying stock to trade for the day, it should target to allocate as close to $1500 as possible without going over that number. It must be deployed solely into that one underlying stock's option chain. Do not open concurrent positions across multiple different tickers on the same day.

When a valid entry signal is generated based on the Morning Stock Selection Protocol, purchase ITM Call Options contracts with a 7 to 14 Days to Expiration (7-14 DTE) window. Size the initial entry position so that a 50% drop in contract premium results in a maximum cash loss of no more than $750. Place a hard premium stop-loss at 50% immediately upon position entry.

Apply a multi-layered, volume-modified profit taking strategy based on market volume and time horizons:

1. Day 1 Final Hour Power Rule: On the first day the position is opened, during the final hour of standard market trading hours (3:00 PM to 4:00 PM EST), evaluate the active option contract premium. If the contract price has gained more than 60% from the initial entry price, immediately execute a market sell order to close the entire position before market close. This rule strictly overrides all other baseline profit targets to eliminate overnight holding risks and avoid potential IV drag.

2. Standard Volume Condition (RVOL is 2.0 or below): If the position survives past Day 1, and the Relative Volume remains at or below 2x the historical average, automatically set a fixed, simultaneous take-profit order to close the entire position when the net profit reaches the exact price of entry (locking in a clean 1:2 risk-to-reward ratio).

3. High-Volume Breakout Condition (RVOL is greater than 2.0): If the Relative Volume expands past 2x the historical average, completely remove the $1,500 fixed profit cap. Activate an automated 3x Average True Range (3x ATR) trailing stop to follow the institutional momentum upward indefinitely, closing the position only when the technical trailing floor is breached.

4. Hard 2-Day Expiration Filter: Regardless of volume or tracking indicators, every position must be fully closed within a maximum window of 2 full trading days. If a position is opened on Day 1, the agent must force-close the entire position by the end of standard trading hours on Day 2. This rule takes absolute priority over all trailing stops.

Execute all risk parameters simultaneously upon position entry.

**Morning Stock Selection Protocol:**

Every trading day, between 6:00 AM and 7:25 AM EST (pre-market), scan the following allowed tickers: GOOG, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, META, AMZN, TSLA, TSM, and SPCX. Evaluate and select the single best underlying asset for the day by applying the following filtering steps in exact sequential order:

Step 1: Catalyst Check  
Identify if any of the five tickers have a fresh, high-impact fundamental catalyst released within the last 12 hours (e.g., an overnight corporate earnings beat, an upgraded institutional price target from a major bank, or a major product release announcement). Give immediate priority to the asset with the strongest news driver.

Step 2: Pre-Market Momentum Rank  
If multiple stocks have positive news, or if no stocks have news, rank the five tickers by their pre-market percentage gain. Identify the ticker showing the cleanest upward technical structure (trading above its pre-market VWAP and 9 EMA).

Step 3: Implied Volatility (IV) Safety Check  
Look at the active 7-14 DTE option chain for the leading stock identified in Step 1 or Step 2. Verify its current Implied Volatility (IV) percentile. If the IV is extremely inflated (above the 80th percentile), pass on that stock to avoid an immediate IV crush, and select the runner-up stock with normal, healthy option pricing instead.

Step 4: Final Day Lock  
At exactly 7:35 AM EST, finalize the selection. Crown the winning asset as the sole 'Underlying Stock of the Day.' Lock all option scanning parameters onto this single ticker's chain, and completely ignore the other tickers for the remainder of the trading session. Open the option position and follow the rest of the trading parameters.
